system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package departs from our playbook on nearly every key position. It also packages several concessions as "agreed" or "settled" when they are not. In particular:

- **Fallbacks:** Two of the Seller's positions (20% cap, 18-month claims period) match our internal fallbacks. Amelia Frost has not given written authority for either, so **neither is available to us** and we should not concede them.
- **Fraud:** The Seller's drafting would subject fraud to the caps and non-reliance clause. This is a non-negotiable red line.
- **Conditions and funds flow:** The Disclosure Letter itself confirms that the Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, bonus funding and title evidence are all **not in place**. The Seller Update presents these as "addressed".

---

## 1. Material departures and recommended pushback

### A. Liability architecture (highest priority)

**1. General cap: Clause 12.1 (Seller: 20% / AUD 4.8m)**
- **Playbook:** start at 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The 20% fallback needs prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft. None exists.
- **Pushback:** reject and restate 25% / AUD 6.0m. Do not signal that 20% is within our range, even informally, until written authority is obtained.

**2. Thresholds: Clause 12.2 (Seller: AUD 25k de minimis, AUD 250k excess-only basket)**
- **Playbook:** AUD 5k de minimis; AUD 50k basket; Seller liable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded.
- **Departure:** the de minimis is 5x ours and the basket is 5x ours. The Seller's basket is also a deductible, not a tipping basket. Combined, these would wipe out a large class of mid-sized claims.
- **Pushback:** reject all three elements. Insist on a tipping basket. Claims below de minimis should also count towards the basket, or at least related claims should be aggregated (we should propose this).

**3. Claims period: Clause 12.3 (Seller: 18 months)**
- **Playbook:** 24 months. The 18-month fallback needs Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given.
- **Pushback:** restate 24 months.

**4. "Limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise": Clauses 12.3 / 13**
- This is a **hidden general-regime override**. It would sweep Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenant claims into the general cap, thresholds and time bar by default.
- **Pushback:** reverse the default. The general limitations should apply only to general Warranty Claims. Expressly exclude Fundamental/Title claims, specific indemnities (Ironquay, bonuses, Riverlark, DD-006 if agreed), covenant breaches, price and payment obligations, and leakage.

**5. Fundamental / Title: Seller wants the same caps and time limits as general warranties**
- **Playbook:** separate regime; 100% cap; at least 6 years; outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Reasoning:** title and capacity go to whether we receive what we pay AUD 24m for. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap them at 20%.
- **Pushback:** reject in full.

**6. Fraud: Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 apply "to all Claims of any nature"**
- **The Seller's draft has no fraud carve-out.** As drafted, the caps, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance would purport to cover fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct.
- **Playbook:** these must be carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. This is **non-waivable**. No one on our side, including the deal team, has authority to concede it.
- **Pushback:**
  - Insert an express, overriding carve-out covering fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct by the Seller, the Company and their officers, employees and advisers.
  - Ensure the non-reliance clause cannot be read as excluding claims for fraudulent misrepresentation, or (to the extent enforceable) statutory claims.

**7. Tax / IP: Seller says "settled under the general regime"**
- **Playbook:** these terms remain **OPEN**. Nothing has been resolved.
- **Pushback:** correct the record in writing. Tax and IP have not been agreed, and we do not accept that they fall under the general cap, thresholds or time limits.
- **Our own position:** we should not over-claim either. Our playbook assumes no unlimited liability. We should propose a separate Tax/IP regime rather than assert unlimited exposure.

### B. Disclosure and knowledge

**8. General disclosure: Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.2; Schedule 7**
- The Seller discloses the entire data room (to 22 Sep 2026), the Accounts, the statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records".
- **Playbook:** specific fair disclosure only. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Pushback:**
  - Delete paras 1.1 and 1.2.
  - Disclosures should qualify only the warranties they fairly and specifically address, with enough detail for us to identify the nature and scope of the matter.
  - The Disclosure Letter should not qualify Fundamental/Title warranties at all.
- **Related point:** the data-room cut-off is 22 Sep 2026, about six weeks ago. Any bring-down disclosure at Completion should be limited and should not cure breaches. We should also ask about the **missing para 1.3**, since the numbering jumps from 1.2 to 1.4.

**9. Para 1.4 non-admission**
- This is acceptable in principle. However, it must not dilute the specific factual statements in paras 2–10, which we will rely on.
- Ensure the clause cannot be used to argue that Bluefen consent or Riverlark discharge are not "required" for Completion purposes. Those are conditions we will set in the SPA.

**10. Buyer knowledge: Clause 8.3**
- **The Seller's draft is the broadest possible form.** It covers anything known to the Buyer *or its advisers*, *or discoverable* from the data room or public records. Combined with the general disclosure, this would make most warranties illusory.
- **Playbook:** delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions.
- **Pushback:** delete Clause 8.3.
  - If any qualifier survives, it must be limited to the **actual** knowledge of named Buyer individuals. It must never cover advisers' knowledge or constructive knowledge.
  - It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
  - Seller-side knowledge qualifiers in the warranties should be tied to named Seller knowledge persons, after reasonable enquiry.

### C. Conditions, Completion and funds flow

**11. Bluefen consent: Clauses 3 / 6.3**
- **The facts are material:** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (around 30%) and has change-control consent under clause 11.2, with conditions in 11.3. The Disclosure Letter (para 2) confirms there is **no final written consent and no evidence that the conditions are satisfied**.
- **Seller's position:** reasonable endeavours, with the condition satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. This is consent-on-delivery and ignores the 11.3 conditions.
- **Pushback:** make it a condition precedent, waivable by the Buyer only. It should require:
  - an effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) written consent under clause 11.2;
  - **evidence before Completion** that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied; and
  - an obligation stronger than reasonable endeavours: all reasonable endeavours, with an information and consultation right for the Buyer and a long-stop date / walk right.
- Calling this "addressed" is inaccurate.

**12. Riverlark facility: Clauses 2 / 7**
- **The facts:** about AUD 3.2m is outstanding, with change-control (8.1) and discharge (9.2) provisions. Para 3 confirms the facility is not repaid and no discharge is included. The Seller offers only a release "following Completion".
- **Playbook:** require a current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. These should include PPSR releases and any deed of release, and must be delivered or held in escrow on payment. A post-completion release needs both an irrevocable undertaking from the lender **and** Amelia Frost's approval. Neither exists.
- **Pushback:** reject the post-completion release.
- **Note:** there is also a change-of-control risk under clause 8.1. If the facility is not discharged at Completion, the change-of-control provision could be triggered. Repayment should be treated as Debt in the debt-free/cash-free calculation.

**13. DD-005 Completion bonuses: funds flow**
- **The facts:** the Seller expressly says the AUD 420,000 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow. Para 5 confirms this, and is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- **Reasoning:** the bonuses are Company liabilities triggered by Completion. If they are not itemised, they fall on the Company, and therefore on us, after Completion. This is exactly the silent exclusion the playbook prohibits.
- **Pushback:**
  - Either include a specific Debt or Transaction Cost line item for AUD 420,000 **plus all triggered on-costs**, deducted from the price, or have the bonuses funded by the Seller.
  - Back this with a specific indemnity outside the general limitations.
  - Request the bonus letters and a calculation of on-costs.

### D. Specific risk items

**14. Ironquay IP: Clause 11.1**
- **The facts:** under DD-004 clause 7.3, transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open. The Seller concedes this is not independent verification, and there is no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment.
- **Seller's position:** the indemnity, limited to the SOW3 payment, is "adequate".
- **Pushback:** broaden the indemnity to cover:
  - any loss from failure of title to, or inability to use, the Ironquay/SOW3 Project Materials;
  - third-party claims; and
  - re-development costs.
- **Preserve the cure path:** payment of all SOW3 fees and delivery of a confirmatory assignment. Ideally make this a pre-Completion deliverable, or retain AUD 180,000 until it is evidenced.
- **Caution:** do not assert that AUD 180,000 is actually unpaid. Do not accept that it is paid either. It is unverified, so request bank or remittance evidence.

**15. DD-006 export/privacy incident: Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6**
- **Seller's characterisation:** "preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material". This is an unsupported conclusion.
- **What para 6 actually says:** access, scope and notification obligations are all unknown.
- **Our position:** we should not overstate the incident either. There is **no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or quantified loss**.
- **Pushback:**
  - Reject the materiality characterisation.
  - Require the Seller to preserve all logs and evidence, continue a proper investigation (including whether it is an eligible data breach under the NDB scheme), give regular written updates, and consult the Buyer before any regulator or individual notification.
  - Consider a specific indemnity or warranty for losses arising from the incident.
  - Do not table a numeric figure until facts emerge.

**16. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): DD-008 / DD-011**
- **Seller's characterisation:** "ordinary-course operating costs". Para 8 is silent on whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course, and asks us to read the three related renewals together.
- **Playbook:** assess the renewals. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Pushback:** do not accept the Seller's characterisation, and do not demand a deduction yet. Request the contracts, the renewal timing, termination rights and accrual treatment. Then decide whether to seek a covenant (no renewal without Buyer consent before Completion), a working-capital adjustment, or nothing.

**17. Title: share register at DD-012**
- **Seller's position:** title "is evidenced by" the DD-012 register. Para 10 itself admits it only identifies the source relied on and that we have not verified it.
- **Playbook:** DD-012 is an internal source supplied by the Seller. It is not independent proof.
- **Pushback:** require independent evidence:
  - ASIC company extract and share-structure history;
  - PPSR search against the Seller and the Company;
  - original share certificates and transfer history;
  - constitution and any shareholder agreement (for pre-emption rights);
  - Seller board resolutions and evidence of authority and capacity;
  - releases of any encumbrances.
- Title warranties sit in the Fundamental regime (see item 5).

### E. Lower-priority items (verify, not concede)

- **Office lease (DD-007):** described as a notification obligation, not a consent requirement. Confirm by reviewing the lease directly, and add a pre-Completion covenant to give the notice.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** described as an assignment restriction that does not require consent on a share sale. Verify that there is no change-of-control or deemed-assignment clause.
- **Disclosure Letter para 11:** the reservation is consistent with our approach. We will evaluate the facts independently.

---

## 2. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | General cap | 20% / 4.8m | **Reject**: 25% / 6.0m. No authority for 20% fallback |
| 2 | Thresholds | 25k / 250k deductible | **Reject**: 5k / 50k tipping basket |
| 3 | Claims period | 18 months | **Reject**: 24 months. No authority for 18-month fallback |
| 4 | "Limitations apply to all Claims" | Default override | **Reject**: confine to general Warranty Claims |
| 5 | Title/Capacity | Same as general | **Reject**: 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket/knowledge |
| 6 | Fraud | No carve-out | **Red line**: full carve-out; non-waivable |
| 7 | Tax/IP | "Settled" | **Correct record**: OPEN; separate regime |
| 8 | Disclosure | Data room + public registers | **Reject**: specific fair disclosure only |
| 9 | Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Blanket, incl. advisers/discoverable | **Delete** |
| 10 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; consent-on-delivery | CP: effective consent + evidence clause 11.3 conditions satisfied |
| 11 | Riverlark | Post-completion release | Payout letter, direct repayment, releases at Completion |
| 12 | Bonuses | Excluded from funds flow | Line item (420k + on-costs) or Seller-funded + indemnity |
| 13 | Ironquay | SOW3-payment-only indemnity | Broaden; keep SOW3 cure; verify 180k |
| 14 | DD-006 | "Not material" | Preservation, investigation, updates; no assumed breach |
| 15 | Sandbar | Ordinary course | Diligence first; no automatic Debt/deduction |
| 16 | Title | DD-012 register | Independent title, encumbrance and authority evidence |

**Process points:**
1. In our cover note, do not describe the Seller's package as "fair and balanced". Correct the record that Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses and Tax/IP are "addressed" or "settled". The Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts the first three.
2. Escalate to Amelia Frost for visibility only. Her approval is required before any movement on the cap or claims period, and before any post-completion Riverlark release. We are not recommending any of these concessions now.
3. Request the following before our mark-up is finalised:
   - updated data-room index and bring-down (the cut-off is now about 6 weeks old);
   - Bluefen clause 11.3 status;
   - Riverlark payout figure;
   - bonus letters and on-cost calculation;
   - Ironquay payment evidence;
   - DD-006 investigation status;
   - Sandbar contracts;
   - independent title searches;
   - the missing Disclosure Letter para 1.3.
=== END ADVICE ===
